extraction.name: RoboBench
extraction.description: RoboBench is a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating multimodal large language models (MLLMs) as embodied brains in robotic manipulation tasks. It defines five dimensions—instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis—spanning 14 capabilities, 25 tasks, and 6092 QA pairs. The benchmark uses realistic data from diverse robot embodiments and introduces an MLLM-as-world-simulator framework for evaluating long-horizon planning.
extraction.creator: Yulin Luo, Chun-Kai Fan, Menghang Dong, Jiayu Shi, Mengdi Zhao, Bo-Wen Zhang, Cheng Chi, Jiaming Liu, Gaole Dai, Rongyu Zhang, Ruichuan An, Kun Wu, Zhengping Che, Shaoxuan Xie, Guocai Yao, Zhongxia Zhao, Pengwei Wang, Guang Liu, Zhongyuan Wang, Tiejun Huang, Shanghang Zhang
extraction.publisher: Peking University, Beijing Academy of Artificial Intelligence
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Datasets were built from open-source and in-house robotic data, enriched with MLLM- and human-provided annotations. Data collection involved extracting frame sequences from high-quality robotic videos, generating structured annotations using Gemini, refining with human annotators, and applying two-stage quality control with 20 professionally trained annotators.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Planning-level failures were synthesized by perturbing correct instructions due to lack of real-world planning failure data.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Open-source and in-house robotic video data, real robot data with type and view metadata, curated static object attributes, robotic execution data from RoboMIND, and high-quality robotic videos from multiple cited sources.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Two-stage quality control: (1) data filtering during construction with general and task-specific filters; (2) post-construction validation by 20 professionally trained annotators checking linguistic clarity, answerability, and correctness. Majority-vote strategy applied: items all models solve correctly are removed; items all models fail undergo manual review. Human annotators also refined Gemini-generated structured annotations (task summaries, step-wise instructions, metadata). Expert labeling for execution-level failures. Human-labeled bounding boxes for task-centric perception.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Majority-vote strategy used to identify and handle items where all models agree (either all correct or all fail), with manual review for the latter.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Gemini used for video segmentation (scene-centric temporal grounding) and generating structured annotations (task summaries, step-wise instructions with timestamps, metadata). GPT used for generating functional properties and distractors for object-centric data. LLMs used for rewriting explicit instructions into implicit demand-based requests.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Planning data primarily focuses on concrete action execution without explicitly distinguishing between left-right arm assignments or positional movements, leading to biases in cross-embodiment planning tasks.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Models struggle with implicit instruction grounding, perception, long-horizon planning, affordance reasoning, and failure diagnosis. Performance drops sharply for uncommon objects, symbolic reasoning, or world knowledge. Execution-level failure analysis is particularly challenging even for humans.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluating Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) as embodied brains for robotic manipulation, covering instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Data augmentation includes: rewriting explicit instructions into implicit demand-based requests using LLMs; synthesizing planning-level failures by perturbing correct instructions (wrong object, missing step, wrong order); applying majority-vote strategy to remove items all models solve correctly and manually reviewing items all models fail; converting explicit task instructions into implicit forms; and mapping natural language steps to predefined function sequences.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data preprocessing includes: standardizing all perception data into multiple-choice QA format; extracting frame sequences from robotic videos as standardized inputs; generating structured annotations (task summaries, step-wise instructions with timestamps, metadata) via Gemini and refining with human annotators; mapping steps into function templates grouped into manipulation or navigation skill lists; applying general and task-specific filters (image quality, task validity, excluding single-arm data from dual-arm tasks); and conducting post-construction validation by 20 trained annotators checking linguistic clarity, answerability, and correctness.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We present RoboBench, a benchmark to systematically evaluate MLLMs as the embodied brain for robotic manipulation. It traces the full execution pipeline across five dimensions—Instruction Comprehension, Perception Reasoning, Generalized Planning, Affordance Prediction, and Failure Analysis—covering 25 tasks with 6092 QA pairs.
